goal: Give every verification check a mode (off, observe or enforce) in the one policy file, so a new check can ship logging what it would have stopped before anyone lets it block work (agent-kit R32, run 2026-11-27-r32-hook-gates).
changed: S2 gains a `checks:` key: a block map of check id to off, observe or enforce. The highest mode any policy file sets wins, a missing id is observe, and an unknown id is an error.

S2 names the known ids (commit-gate, stop-checks, spec-drift, receipts, test-guard), the rule that an enforced check may let an action through after two stops in one session and record why (a gate never does), and where an observe log goes: a would-block lesson in the machine's weekly flags run.
S2's agentfiles changes and acceptance criteria gain the merge, the policy check and a test for them. No ledger code changes: the ledger reads only security.redact_patterns from a policy file.

claims.claim: The ledger's policy reader still reads redact patterns from a policy file that has a checks: block, and ignores the block.
claims.check: read_policy_patterns on a copy of a synced ~/.agents/policy.yaml with a checks: block appended, once with redact_patterns: [] and once with one pattern
claims.remaining: agentfiles doesn't accept the key yet; that is the run's next unit.

claims.claim: The test suite passes with the spec change.
claims.check: uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python -m unittest discover -s tests (the repo needs 3.10 or newer)

next.item: agentfiles parses and merges checks: and writes it at sync
next.why_now: Until agentfiles accepts the key, a profile can't set a mode and bstack's hooks read only the default.
next.impact: Beau moves a check from observe to enforce with one profile line and agentfiles sync.

release.note: The policy spec gives verification checks a mode: off, observe or enforce. New checks ship in observe.
